description: Steady A2 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Stamp has /æ/. Stump has /ʌ/, step has /ɛ/, and stomp has /ɑ/ in General American.
Fresh has the short /ɛ/ vowel. Flash has /æ/; the other options do not match the spoken vowel.
Drum has /ʌ/. Dream has /i/, while dram has /æ/; droom is not a standard spelling.
Jacket begins with /dʒ/. Yacket begins with /j/, packet with /p/, and shacket is not the standard word.
Thin begins with unvoiced /θ/. Tin begins with /t/, then with voiced /ð/, and sin with /s/.
Queen begins with /kw/. Clean begins with /kl/, keen with /k/, and green with /gr/.
Cough ends with /f/. Cove ends with /v/, coat with /t/, and code with /d/.
Bench ends with /tʃ/, written ch. Bend ends with /d/, belt with /t/, and best with /t/ plus /s/.
Prize ends with voiced /z/. Price ends with /s/, pride with /d/, and prime with /m/.
Float uses oa to spell /oʊ/. Flout has /aʊ/, fleet has /i/, and flote is not the standard spelling.
Bright uses igh to spell /aɪ/. Brite is a nonstandard spelling, and the other choices do not spell the target.
Knight begins with a silent k and has the /aɪ/ sound. Night sounds the same but is a different word and spelling; kite and knit sound different.
